events.text: I'll systematically search for the latest versions of each study/report cited in the draft. Let me run all searches in parallel.
Now I have enough information to assess all seven sources. Let me also check whether there is a newer GEM Report (2023 or 2024) that would supersede the 2020 one cited as [5].

I now have sufficient information to produce the full assessment. Here is my analysis of each source:

**[1] Hunt et al. 2025 (Campbell SR)** — The draft's primary source. Published 6 February 2025, Campbell Systematic Reviews 21, e70016. This is the final review that superseded the 2021 protocol. No further update found. CURRENT.

**[2] Mendoza & Heymann 2022** — Published July 2022, IJDDE 71(3):299–316. The draft says it could not hold this source, so draws nothing from it. No update found beyond the 2022 publication. UNKNOWN (not held; no update confirmed or denied).

**[3] Ahmed et al. 2022 (Campbell EGM)** — Published November 2022, Campbell SR 18, e1287. A corrigendum was published February 2023 (Campbell SR 19, e1315). The draft acknowledges a correction it could not read and draws nothing from this source. The correction is confirmed to exist. UNKNOWN (correction not read; figures not verified).

**[4] Saran, White & Kuper 2020 (Campbell EGM)** — Published January 2020, Campbell SR 16, e1070. A corrigendum was published July 2020 (same volume, issue 3). The draft acknowledges a correction it could not hold and draws nothing from this source. The correction is confirmed to exist. UNKNOWN (correction not read; figures not verified).

**[5] UNESCO GEM Report 2020** — The draft says it could not hold this source and draws nothing from it. The 2020 GEM Report on inclusion is a standalone thematic edition; subsequent GEM Reports (2023: Technology; 2024/5: Leadership) cover different themes and do not supersede the 2020 inclusion-specific content. CURRENT for its thematic scope (inclusion), though the draft draws nothing from it.

**[6] UNESCO Guide for Ensuring Inclusion and Equity in Education 2017** — Published 2017, 46 pp. The UNESCO page shows "Last update: 25 November 2025" but this appears to be a metadata/webpage update, not a new edition of the guide itself; all citations and library records consistently point to the 2017 publication with no revised edition found. UNKNOWN (cannot positively confirm no revised edition exists, but no revised edition was found).

**[7] Hunt et al. 2021 Protocol** — Published October 2021, Campbell SR 17, e1197. PubMed explicitly flags this as updated by the 2025 review (e70016). The draft uses this source only for background/protocol-level statements (what the protocol noted about gaps in prior evidence), not for any effectiveness findings. The 2025 review is the update of this protocol. The draft correctly treats [7] as the protocol and [1] as the completed review. CURRENT (used appropriately as protocol, not as a source of effectiveness findings).

I found nothing to object to in the Ethiopia and Cambodia sentences.

- **Ethiopia:** The figures and outcomes match the guide's Box 11. That box says the approach "led to improvements in inclusive education practice by service-providers, better physical accessibility for learners, increased enrolment for children with disabilities and a better learning environment for all students". It cites Murenzi and Mebratu (2013).
- **Cambodia:** The quoted phrasing matches Box 13, p. 27.
- **Limits of my check:** I could not open the PDF itself. I checked these passages against copies of the guide that came up in search, so the section locators are approximate.

A 2025 Campbell systematic review concluded that a range of individual-level interventions improve educational outcomes among people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries, with 12 of 18 interventions showing a significant effect on 'Skills for learning'. However, all but one included study was rated low confidence in its findings [1].
